chain.g: divinity, deity, the nature of a god

ety.text: From Middle French deité, from Latin deitās.

senses.d: Synonym of divinity: the state, position, or fact of being a god.
ex: Thou seest all, yet none at all sees thee: / All that is by the working of thy Deitee.

senses.d: A supernatural divine being; a god or goddess.
ex: Every act of a Roman, from birth to death, from dawn to night, was controlled and supervised by some presiding deity.
The crux of monotheism is not only belief in a single deity but belief in a deity who is different from everything else.

chain.g: divinity, deity, the nature of a god

ety.text: Apocopation of earlier deitade, deitate, from Latin deitātem.

Inherited from Old Spanish dios, from Latin deus (“god, deity”), from Old Latin deivos (“god, deity”), from Proto-Italic *deiwos (“god, deity”), from Proto-Indo-European *deywós (“god, deity”), from *dyew- (“sky, heaven”). The form in -os continues the Latin nominative, not the expected accusative as in Ladino dio.
